content.content:
1	# CabinetMaker — Project Plan
2	
3	**Date:** 2026-10-10
4	
5	**Stack:** C# · Blazor Server · .NET 10 · Entity Framework Core 10 · MySQL (primary) / SQL Server (supported) · Bootstrap · Docker (Linux)
6	
7	## 1. Project Purpose
8	
9	CabinetMaker is a professional-grade, multi-tenant design tool for cabinet makers and furniture builders. Its core job is to capture, organize, and calculate measurements for cabinet projects — from a single unit to a complete kitchen or custom furniture piece — and produce accurate cut lists, material estimates, and project summaries.
10	
11	Two foundational primitives underpin everything else:
12	
13	1. A **database-driven, unit-agnostic measurement system** — every dimension, mass, or volume flows through a unified conversion engine, preventing metric/imperial collisions and supporting tape-measure-accurate fractional snapping.
14	
15	2. A **tenant isolation model** — every piece of data is scoped to the tenant it belongs to, enforced at the database layer, invisible to application code.
16	
17	## 2. Infrastructure & Deployment
18	
19	### 2.1 Docker / Linux Hosting
20	
21	The application is packaged as a Docker container and can run on any Linux Docker host (self-hosted, VPS, cloud VM). No Azure-specific or Windows-specific dependencies are permitted.
22	
23	```
24	docker-compose.yml (development)
25	  web       — CabinetMaker.Web container (port 8080)
26	  db        — MySQL 8.x container (port 3306)
27	
28	Dockerfile  (multi-stage)
29	  Stage 1 (build): mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0
30	  Stage 2 (runtime): mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0-bookworm-slim
31	```
32	
33	All configuration (connection strings, admin seed credentials) is supplied via environment variables. No secrets are baked into the image.
34	
35	Two compose files are maintained:
36	
37	| File | Purpose |
38	|---|---|
39	| `docker-compose.yml` | Local development — builds from source, exposes all ports, ships with safe dev defaults, includes dbgate DB admin UI on port 8081 |
40	| `docker-compose.prod.yml` | Production — pulls a pre-built registry image, binds web to `127.0.0.1:8080` only, no default passwords, `restart: always`, no DB admin UI |
41	
42	### 2.1.1 Production Reverse Proxy
43	
44	In production the app sits behind an existing nginx reverse proxy (Nginx Proxy Manager or equivalent). The app container binds only to `127.0.0.1:8080` — it is never directly internet-facing. The proxy handles SSL termination, domain assignment, and certificate management. Deploying a new version is: push image to registry → pull on server → `docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d` → register the `127.0.0.1:8080` upstream in the proxy console. No nginx container is included in the production compose file.
45	
46	### 2.2 Database Provider Abstraction
47	
48	**Primary: MySQL 8.x** (Oracle official `MySql.EntityFrameworkCore` provider). **Also supported: SQL Server** (Microsoft EF Core provider). The active provider is selected at startup from a single config value:
49	
50	```
51	# appsettings.json / environment variable
52	"DatabaseProvider": "MySql"   // or "SqlServer"
53	```
54	
55	A `DatabaseProviderFactory` extension method in DAL registers the correct `DbContextOptions` based on this value:
56	
57	```csharp
58	// DAL/Extensions/DatabaseProviderExtensions.cs
59	services.AddDbContext<CabinetMakerDbContext>(options =>
60	{
61	    if (provider == "MySql")
62	        options.UseMySQL(connectionString);
63	    else
64	        options.UseSqlServer(connectionString);
65	});
66	```
67	
68	**Provider differences to account for:**
69	
70	| Feature | MySQL (Pomelo) | SQL Server |
71	|---|---|---|
72	| JSON columns | `JSON` type, `.HasColumnType("json")` | `nvarchar(max)` or `json` (SQL Server 2022+) |
73	| GUIDs | `char(36)` or `binary(16)` | `uniqueidentifier` |
74	| Auto-increment | `AUTO_INCREMENT` | `IDENTITY` |
75	| Migrations | Separate migration sets per provider, or provider-aware migrations |
76	
77	Migrations are kept in separate folders: `DAL/Migrations/MySql/` and `DAL/Migrations/SqlServer/`. A CLI helper script selects the correct migration context at design time.
78	
79	### 2.3 Timezone Architecture
80	
81	All temporal data in the system must be unambiguous about which instant in time it refers to. This matters especially for future-dated succession records (§5.1) where a user schedules a material change to take effect "at midnight on Nov 1" — midnight in *whose* timezone needs a definitive answer.
82	
83	#### Rule: UTC everywhere in the database and server
84	
85	- **Database:** All `DATETIME` columns store UTC values. The DB server timezone is irrelevant and must never influence stored values. MySQL `TIMESTAMP` type is specifically avoided because it auto-converts using the server timezone — `DATETIME` is used instead.
86	- **C# domain model:** All temporal properties use `DateTime`, always in UTC. The convention is enforced at the service boundary — every value written to a `DateTime` field must be UTC. Reading from DB always returns UTC. `DateTime.Now` is never used anywhere in the codebase.
87	- **EF Core convention:** A global value converter enforces `DateTimeKind.Utc` on all `DateTime` properties at the DbContext boundary, converting any non-UTC value on read and throwing on write if `Kind != Utc`.
88	- **Server-side "now":** All services obtain the current instant through an injected `TimeProvider`. Never call `DateTime.UtcNow` or `DateTime.Now` directly.
89	
90	```csharp
91	// Production — registered once in Program.cs
92	services.AddSingleton(TimeProvider.System);
93	
94	// In any service that needs the current time
95	public class RecordSuccessionService(TimeProvider timeProvider)
96	{
97	    private DateTime Now => _timeProvider.GetUtcNow().DateTime;
98	}
99	```
100
